# Perform Hartley's Fmax test

<small>Source: [`man/performHartleyFmaxTest.Rd`](https://github.com/DiogoRibeiro7/heteroTests/blob/main/man/performHartleyFmaxTest.Rd) · Help: `?performHartleyFmaxTest`</small>

Compares the maximum and minimum group residual variances using Hartley's maximum F-ratio distribution.

## Usage

```r
performHartleyFmaxTest(model, data = NULL, group)
```

## Arguments

`model`
:   A fitted `lm` object.

`data`
:   The data frame `model` was fitted to, or `NULL`, the default. The residuals and weights are read from the fit itself, and `group` from the rows of `data` that hold the observations of the fit. Without `data` it is read from the model frame of `model`, which holds it only when it is a variable of the model under its own name (`x`, not `log(x)`); a grouping variable the model does not use needs `data`. Since 0.16.0, data that are given are matched to the observations of the fit: rows with row names of their own by name, in any order; rows that only number themselves (a tibble, a data.table, a data frame whose row names were reset) by the row numbers of the fit, or in the order of the fit when they hold one row per observation. The rows the fit dropped may be there or not. Data whose rows cannot be shown to hold the observations of the fit are refused; see [`test_results`](test_results.md).

`group`
:   Name of the grouping variable.

## Value

An object of class `htest` containing the Fmax statistic, number of groups, reference degrees of freedom and p-value.

## Details

The statistic is \(F_{max}=\max_j s_j^2/\min_j s_j^2\). Under normality and equal group sizes its null distribution is the maximum F-ratio distribution for \(k\) independent mean squares with common degrees of freedom, evaluated with `SuppDists::pmaxFratio()`. If group sizes differ, the function warns and rounds the mean group size, then subtracts one, to obtain an approximate common integer degrees of freedom.

## Supported models

It accepts an `lm` and a `glm` with the Gaussian family and the identity link, unweighted
or with positive weights, a `fitWLS()` fit and, since 0.16.0, a rank-deficient fit, which it
tests on the estimable part of its design: it gives the value of the same model fitted without the
aliased columns. It refuses a `glm` of another family or link, a `survey::svyglm()` fit, a
fit with a zero weight, a coefficient that is not finite for another reason, and `data` that
lack rows or variables of the fit.
It refuses a multivariate `lm` ("needs a model with one response"), since 0.16.0; before, it
stopped with a coercion error. An `mgcv::gam()` fit is tested as before 0.16.0, with penalised
smooth terms too: the test reads its residuals and does not fit it again, so it does not take them
for least-squares residuals (decision 37 of the design of the model context); since 0.16.0 its
observations are matched to the rows of `data` by the row names of its model frame. Before,
they were matched by position, since the residuals of a `gam` carry no names, and `data`
with the rows of the fit in another order gave a wrong value.
Which model each test accepts, and why, is set out in
[`test_results`](test_results.md), under *Supported models*.

## References

Hartley, H. O. (1950). The maximum F-ratio as a short-cut test for heterogeneity of variance. *Biometrika*, 37(3/4), 308–312.

## Examples

```r
 set.seed(1701)
 n <- 20
 d <- data.frame(g = factor(rep(letters[1:3], each = n)), x = rnorm(3 * n))
 d$y <- 1 + d$x + rnorm(3 * n)
 m <- lm(y ~ x, data = d)
 performHartleyFmaxTest(m, d, "g")
```
